subject: Clarify charges during midnight timezone rollover (May billing window)
messages:
From: Evan Torres <evan.torres@fastlane.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@fastlane.ai>, billing@fastlane.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 00:12:00 -0400
Subject: Unexpected charge during midnight rollover — May billing window

Hi Olga —

We noticed an unexpected ~34k token charge in yesterday's invoice that appears to have been billed to our production entity between 23:55 and 00:05 UTC on May 17/18. Our team uses a strict daily cutoff at 00:00 UTC; looks like something was counted into the next billing day during the timezone rollover.

I've attached a small CSV with the request ids and timestamps as we logged them (usage_export_20270517.csv). Can you confirm what your ingestion window and cutoff logic was during that period? If this was a collection-window edge-case on Redwood's side, we'd like a remediation path or provisional credit while we reconcile — this is material to our monthly burn.

Thanks — appreciate a quick turnaround.

Evan Torres
Head of Platform, FastLane AI
E: evan.torres@fastlane.ai
T: +1 415-555-0199

[attachment: usage_export_20270517.csv (3 rows referenced)]

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Evan Torres <evan.torres@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 02:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Unexpected charge during midnight rollover — May billing window

Hi Evan —

Thanks for flagging and for the CSV — sending this internally so we can get a quick root cause and propose next steps. A couple quick asks while we investigate:

- Can you confirm the timezone your logs are in (UTC vs local)? The times in your export look like local timestamps that may have been converted.
- Do you have request ids for the largest tokens in that window (we can match request_id -> router shard traces)?

Ben / Connor — can you look at the ingest and billing-window logic for 2027-05-17 23:50:00 UTC through 2027-05-18 00:10:00 UTC? Cross-check the KV-cache eviction events and any scheduled batch flushes; also check whether the rollout for the prefix-aggregation change completed on May 17 (there was a small rollout at ~22:30 UTC).

I'll hold off on a formal credit until we confirm the cause; we may offer a provisional adjustment if it's on our side. Evan, we'll loop back within 24 hours with evidence and a remediation plan.

Olga Petrov
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 206-555-0127

[internal note: attaching signed PO FastLane signed_po_0427.pdf to the ticket for accounting reference]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:40:00 -0400
Subject: RE: Unexpected charge during midnight rollover — May billing window

Quick summary from infra after initial triage:

- We confirmed a scheduled prefix-aggregation flush job ran at 00:01:22 UTC on 2027-05-18 that batched a small backlog of streaming requests into billing buckets. Normally these are applied to 23:59:59 UTC cutoffs, but an internal race condition in the window-assigner can tag late flushes to the immediate next window when flush timestamp > window_cutoff_ts and router_shard latency > 500ms.
- On 2027-05-17 22:30 UTC we rolled a change to shard-routing that reduced tail latency; the rollout was gradual and one shard (shard-7) had a delayed config apply and experienced a 600–1,200ms tail for ~20 minutes. That aligns with the user-provided times once we convert their local tz to UTC.
- We can match 2 of Evan's request_ids to our traces; attached is a sanitized snapshot (ingest-window-snapshot.json) showing the per-request assignment and the rule that bumped them into the May 18 window.

Suggested remediation path:
1) Offer a provisional credit for the disputed ~34k tokens while we run a full backfill to determine total affected count.
2) Patch the window-assigner to prefer original request_received_ts when assigning to cutoffs (rollback is low-risk).
3) Run a retroactive billing reclassification for affected requests (we can backdate to May 17 window) and send a corrected invoice / credit note.

If Finance approves the provisional credit we can apply a contra-charge now and adjust once backfill completes. Connor: can you estimate run time for the backfill and a safe SLA for a corrected invoice?

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Billing Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

[attachment: ingest-window-snapshot.json (sanitized trace, 2 matched request ids)]

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Evan Torres <evan.torres@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, billing@fastlane.ai
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Unexpected charge during midnight rollover — May billing window

Hi Evan / Maya —

Thank you for your patience. We investigated the timestamps and infra traces and confirmed that a small subset of streaming requests from FastLane were assigned to the May 18 billing window due to a race in the window-assigner tied to a delayed shard config roll. Ben has attached a sanitized snapshot that maps two of your request_ids to the behavior we saw.

What we propose:
- Immediate provisional credit: Redwood will credit the disputed ~34k tokens to your May invoice as a provisional adjustment while we complete a full backfill. This will appear as a line item "Timezone rollover provisional credit" on your June statement.
- Technical fix: We'll push the window-assigner patch tomorrow (May 21) to ensure original request_received_ts is the primary key for cutoff assignment.
- Final reconciliation: Backfill will run within 72 hours after the patch completes; we'll reclassify affected requests and issue a corrected invoice/credit note if the provisional amount differs.

Please confirm you accept the provisional credit path and we will route this to Finance and apply the contra at the next statement run. Attached for your records: signed PO (signed_po_0427.pdf) and the sanitized ingest snapshot.

If you prefer a manual credit today instead of waiting for the statement cycle, we can expedite — let me know.

Olga Petrov
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com | +1 206-555-0127
